title: Personal OKR draft — Jasper Kim Q2 2026
content:
Notes / draft OKRs for Q2 2026 - working doc.

Context:
- Role: Senior Software Engineer, serving-runtime. Focus on reducing latency and platform robustness for hosted API, and finishing KV cache feature for prefix reuse.
- High-level goal: Make day-to-day latency and cost predictable for small-to-medium workloads while keeping P95/P99 under tight SLOs.

Objective 1: Reduce tail latency and variability for text-generation endpoints
Key results:
- KR1.1: Reduce P99 latency (1k token requests) for hosted-api small model tier by 15% vs baseline (baseline = 320ms -> target ~272ms).
- KR1.2: Reduce P95 variance (stddev) by 25% measured over weekly sample of 10k requests.
- KR1.3: Ship automated fallbacks for model-variant routing so 99.9% of requests succeed without human intervention (monitor success rate).

Initiatives / Plan:
- Finish KV cache integration with continuous batching (primary deliverable: L1 patch + perf tests by end of May).
- Add adaptive batching heuristics: prototype and A/B on 10% traffic.
- Work with infra on kernel selection tuning for A100 vs H100 profiles (measure & commit changes).
- Create dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 and variance; add alert for P99 regressions > 10% week-over-week.

Risks & open questions:
- Potential regressions for long-context workloads when introducing more aggressive batching. Need canary and rollback plan.
- Dependence on infra team timeline for kernel updates (blocking risk).
- Need clearer SLA definition with product for "small model tier" - confirm exact model set and token budgets.

Objective 2: Improve developer velocity for rollout and observability of serving changes
Key results:
- KR2.1: Reduce median time from PR merge to safe canary rollout from 3d -> <24h.
- KR2.2: Increase number of canary rollouts executed per week (team) from 1 -> 3 (by automating routine steps).
- KR2.3: Write 2 runbooks and 1 postmortem template for common regressions (latency spike, memory leak).

Initiatives / Plan:
- Automate canary orchestration scripts (copy existing manual steps into simple workflow).
- Add tracing hooks and synthetic traffic generator for quick validation pre-rollout.
- Pair with SRE on runbook drafts; schedule 2 knowledge-transfer sessions.

Personal growth / team contributions:
- Mentor: 1-2 engineers on perf debugging (pair weekly).
- Docs: finish "KV cache design notes" and a short "how to measure P99 change" guide.

Weekly check-in template (to paste into weekly notes):
- This week (what I shipped):
  - e.g., "Merged KV cache basic integration into canary branch; end-to-end tests passing; perf harness setup."
- Metrics update (short):
  - p50/p95/p99 snapshot vs baseline (link to dashboard).
- Blockers / needs:
  - e.g., "Need kernel tuning from infra; blocked on CORP-456."
- Plans for next week:
  - e.g., "Finish adaptive batching prototype; schedule canary on 10% traffic; write runbook draft."

Quick TODOs (short, actionable):
- [ ] Confirm small-model tier list with product (ask Priya).
- [ ] Add synthetic traffic config and run nightly perf job.
- [ ] Draft runbook for latency spikes and share with SRE.
- [ ] Schedule kernel tuning sync with infra (include perf numbers).

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Focus on measurable KRs; avoid vague "improve performance" phrasing.
- Keep rollout safe: canary -> monitor 15m -> ramp -> monitor 60m -> full.
- If batching increases p99 for short requests, add fast-path bypass for <50-token requests.

Links / references:
- Confluence: SERVE-optimizer-q2 (design notes).
- GitHub: repo/PR#456 (KV cache WIP).
- Jira: SRV-1234 (kernel tuning task).

Questions to bring to 1:1 with manager:
- Are the KR targets aggressive enough?
- Where should I prioritize developer velocity vs latency wins?
- Any preference on pairing assignments for mentoring?

Status: DRAFT - put into draft OKRs doc for feedback. Asking Maya + Priya to review and comment.
